question.:question/problem: Let $A$ be a $7\times 7$ matrix. If $B=\{{b}_{1}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(A)$, find $\text{dim(Null}(A)).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=7,$ and since $B$ is formed by $1$ vector, $\text{rank}(A)=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ 1+\text{nullity}(A) & =7 \\ \text{nullity}(A) & =7-1 \\ \text{dim(Null}(A)) & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=4,$ since this is the number of components in each of the vectors of the null space. 

Also, since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\,|\,\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R\}
$$

we conclude that $\text{nullity}(A)=2.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ \text{rank}(A)+2 & =4 \\ \text{rank}(A) & =4-2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
